mechanisms.name: rotationPolicy default flips from Never to Always: root CA Certificate cert-manager/mesh-root-ca (explicit rotationPolicy)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: **Unaffected.** The behaviour is the same before and after.
resourcesConsumers: leaf Secrets' ca.crt (copy of root cert)
mechanisms.mechanism: If the root had defaulted to Always, its next renewal (at about 8040h of its 8760h life) would have issued a new root key. Any leaf not yet reissued would then chain to the old root key, and the mTLS between checkout and ledger would break.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The prod overlay patch platform/pki/overlays/prod/mesh-root-ca-prod.yaml pins rotationPolicy: Never; the rendered output for both versions shows the merged object with rotationPolicy: Never, so the value is identical before and after. Any other environment that builds from pki/base without that overlay would not have this protection.
citedEvidence: rendered/from.yaml:13906 and rendered/to.yaml:14034 show rotationPolicy: Never in the final merged object
assumptions: Repo state reflects the live cluster; the assessor only saw the repo, not the cluster
ORIENTATION.md says the repo is complete, but this could not be verified
missingEvidence: Confirmation that the live Certificate/mesh-root-ca in cert-manager really has rotationPolicy: Never and that Argo CD is synced and not out of sync on that field
Whether staging or dev builds the PKI from pki/base without the prod overlay
recommendedValidation: Confirm live Certificate/mesh-root-ca has rotationPolicy: Never and Argo CD is synced on that field
Check whether staging/dev builds PKI from pki/base without the prod overlay; if so its root CA would rotate on the new default (a place to see the failure mode, but also something to fix)
Keep the root CA's Never; consider moving it into the base so other overlays inherit it

mechanisms.name: rotationPolicy default flips from Never to Always: leaf Certificates ledger-tls and checkout-tls (rely on the default)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: Certificates that rely on the default (affected)
resourcesConsumers: ledger nginx (ledger-deployment.yaml, ledger.conf) mounting Secret ledger-tls
mechanisms.mechanism: Before, the key was reused on every renewal; after, a new ECDSA P-256 key is generated on every reissue. Nothing is reissued by the upgrade itself; the first key rotation happens at each certificate's next renewal after the controller upgrade (duration 720h, renewBefore 240h, roughly every 20 days) or at any manual reissue (spec edit, Secret deletion, cmctl renew). For checkout, curl re-reads files on every call and could in theory read tls.crt and tls.key on opposite sides of the swap, costing at most one failed call ("ledger call failed") per rotation, self-healing within 30s; this could not happen before 1.18. ledger nginx keeps serving the old pair until restarted (pre-existing, not caused by the new default).
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: No consumer depends on the keys staying stable: ledger checks client certs against ca.crt only and pins no key or cert; checkout verifies ledger against its own ca.crt and pins nothing; no key hashes, allow-lists, SPKI pins or external copies found (checked by grep and by reading every file under env/). Kubelet updates the Secret volume atomically. Because the signing CA is unchanged, new leaves chain to the same root and are accepted. Rated low risk.
citedEvidence: apps/payments/base/ledger-certificate.yaml and checkout-certificate.yaml: privateKey block with algorithm and size only, no rotationPolicy; duration: 720h, renewBefore: 240h
env/platform/cert-manager/values.yaml has no config.featureGates and no controller extraArgs

rendered/to.yaml controller args only --v=2, --cluster-resource-namespace, --leader-election-namespace, --acme-http01-solver-image, --max-concurrent-challenges, so DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways is on by default
clusters/prod/cert-manager.yaml pins targetRevision: v1.17.2 (only place the version is set)
ledger-deployment.yaml, ledger.conf (nginx reads /tls/tls.crt and /tls/tls.key, checks client certs against ca.crt)
grep and reading every file under env/ found no other consumers

Repo reflects live cluster state (only the repo was seen)
The checkout mismatch window is theoretical ("could in theory")

mechanisms.name: Issuers: mesh-ca ClusterIssuer and selfsigned-bootstrap
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: mesh-ca is a CA issuer reading the root Secret and does not use rotationPolicy; selfsigned-bootstrap is an issuer, and issuers have no rotationPolicy.
assumptions: selfsigned-bootstrap was not reviewed in depth

mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: The CRD diff is additive and cosmetic for this field.

mechanisms.name: Feature gate (DefaultPrivateKeyRotationPolicyAlways) removed in 1.19
mechanisms.mechanism: Longer term, the feature gate goes away in 1.19, so the chart feature-gate opt-out disappears and the choice has to be made explicitly before then.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: Setting rotationPolicy explicitly on ledger-tls and checkout-tls survives the removal of the feature gate in 1.19.
recommendedValidation: Do not use the chart feature-gate opt-out as the long-term answer; set rotationPolicy explicitly

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions: the upgrade is rated low risk, but the leaf rotation behaviour should be decided explicitly in git before or with the upgrade (rotationPolicy: Never to keep current behaviour, or Always only after the unknowns are checked). Keep the root CA's Never, do not rely on the feature-gate opt-out, and complete the live-state, renewal-timing, out-of-repo consumer, staging and reload checks before proceeding.
overall.quote: Explicitly decide the leaf behaviour in git before or with the upgrade, rather than relying on the default
